main_text.p: se præparat ad occidendum; adeoque occidendi hominis gratiâ, cum telo obambulat. Verùm qui ense aut ferro aliquem petit, licet nondum percusserit, se ad occidendum præ-parasse dicetur. Igitur & ille Wesemb. Consil. 19.n.14. ibid. alii.jure repellitur. Neque enim tantùm tenemur obviare malo, quod est in actu, verùm etiam quod est in potentiâ, & l.3.D.de Just.& jur.l.1.§. vim vi D.de vi &viar-mat.l.1. Cod. Vn/ de vi.quidem proximâ, quæ facile in actum deduci posset. Ut probato insultu, & provocatione, à parte ejus qui resistit, vel etiam occidit, justa defensio, probata dicatur. 3. page.notes: Printed notes in the left margin are split at the lines where they stand: the first note block (Wesemb. / Consil. / 19.n.14. / ibid. alii.) stands beside "jure repellitur"; the second block (l.3.D.de Juft.& / jur.l.1.§. / vim vi / D.de vi / &viar- / mat.l.1. / Cod. Vn/ / de vi.) runs down beside lines 11 to 16. Shown as printed, with s read as s and "Juft" as Just. Doubtful: "Vn/" in "Cod. Vn/" may be "Vn." (marked as read); page number "154" where the "1" looks like "r" (marked [?]). The line "re-" at the foot is taken as the catchword, since it stands alone at the right below the last line. Printed "poteft" is read as potest, "fiquidem" as siquidem, "eft" as est, following the rule for long s.
